title: US Health Officials Face Questions Over Missing Measles Data
subtitle: Government agencies are excluding recent deaths from official counts, causing confusion and concern among medical experts.

summary.en: Recent measles deaths in Pennsylvania are not being included in official US government health reports. Federal officials have questioned the accuracy of these reports, leading to a public disagreement. Experts warn that this unusual move could harm the relationship between state and national health agencies. The debate highlights growing tensions over vaccine policy and public health communication. Meanwhile, families affected by the outbreak are sharing their tragic experiences.
summary.zh: 近期賓夕法尼亞州的麻疹死亡病例未被納入美國政府的官方衛生報告中。聯邦官員對這些報告的準確性提出質疑，引發了公開爭論。專家警告，這種罕見的舉動可能會損害州與聯邦衛生機構之間的關係。這場辯論凸顯了疫苗政策與公共衛生溝通方面日益緊張的局勢。與此同時，受疫情影響的家庭也分享了他們悲痛的經歷。

paragraphs.en: A serious disagreement is growing between state and federal health officials in the United States following the deaths of two people from measles in Pennsylvania. While state officials confirmed these deaths in August, the federal Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has decided not to include them in its national count. This decision has caused confusion among medical experts and raised questions about how the government handles health data during an outbreak.
paragraphs.zh: 在賓夕法尼亞州發生兩起麻疹死亡病例後，美國州政府與聯邦衛生官員之間的分歧日益嚴重。儘管州政府官員在八月證實了這些死亡案例，但聯邦疾病管制暨預防中心（CDC）卻決定不將其納入全國統計數據。這項決定不僅讓醫學專家感到困惑，也引發了外界對於政府在疫情期間如何處理衛生數據的質疑。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian, the CDC released a note explaining that it is reviewing additional information about the circumstances of the deaths. The agency stated that it is not yet clear if measles was the direct cause of death or if the individuals died from other health issues while they happened to be infected with the virus. This approach is highly unusual. Typically, when states report cases of infectious diseases to the CDC, the federal agency includes them in its national tally without questioning the state's findings unless the state asks for extra help.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，疾病管制暨預防中心發布了一份說明，表示正在審查關於這些死亡案例情況的額外資訊。該機構指出，目前尚不清楚麻疹是否為直接死因，還是死者在感染病毒的同時，其實是死於其他健康問題。這種處理方式極為罕見。通常情況下，當各州向疾病管制暨預防中心通報傳染病病例時，聯邦機構會直接將其納入全國統計，除非該州主動請求額外協助，否則不會質疑州政府的調查結果。

paragraphs.en: Debra Houry, a former chief medical officer at the CDC, told The Guardian that this situation is very different from how the agency handled three measles-related deaths in Texas and New Mexico last year. She noted that those cases were reported by the states and immediately included in the national data. Houry warned that by choosing to review these cases in such a public way, the CDC risks damaging its collaborative relationship with state health departments. She described the communication coming from the CDC as political rather than focused on managing the health crisis.
paragraphs.zh: 曾任疾病管制暨預防中心首席醫療官的黛布拉·豪里（Debra Houry）告訴《衛報》，這種情況與該機構去年處理德州和新墨西哥州三起麻疹相關死亡案例的方式大相逕庭。她指出，當時那些案例由各州通報後，便立即被納入全國數據中。豪里警告，疾病管制暨預防中心選擇以如此公開的方式審查這些案例，恐將損害其與各州衛生部門的合作關係。她形容疾病管制暨預防中心目前的溝通方式更偏向政治考量，而非專注於應對衛生危機。

paragraphs.en: Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), has taken a strong position on the matter. In a recent interview, he suggested that the reports of the two deaths in Pennsylvania were fabricated. He also claimed that there have only been three measles deaths in America over the last ten years, a statement that does not match the official records of three deaths from last year alone. Kennedy argued that the media and some politicians are trying to scare the public about infectious diseases, and he stated that he wants to focus attention on foodborne illnesses instead.
paragraphs.zh: 美國衛生及公共服務部（HHS）部長小羅伯特·甘迺迪（Robert F. Kennedy Jr.）對此事採取了強硬立場。在最近的一次採訪中，他暗示賓夕法尼亞州的兩起死亡報告是捏造的。他還聲稱過去十年美國僅有三起麻疹死亡病例，這項說法與去年一年就有三起死亡的官方紀錄並不相符。甘迺迪主張，媒體與部分政客試圖利用傳染病恐嚇大眾，並表示他希望將注意力轉向食源性疾病。

paragraphs.en: The human impact of the outbreak remains a major concern. The Atlantic reported on an Amish couple in Lancaster County whose newborn son died shortly after birth. The mother had been suffering from a severe case of measles and went into labor one month early. Although the baby was born with a pulse, he was not breathing, and paramedics were unable to save him. The mother explained that she was worried about the rising number of measles cases in her community but could not get the vaccine because she was pregnant. Vaccines are medicines that help the body fight off specific diseases, and they are generally recommended for most people to prevent outbreaks.
paragraphs.zh: 疫情對個人造成的影響仍是主要關切點。《大西洋》（The Atlantic）雜誌報導了蘭開斯特郡一對阿米希夫婦的悲劇，他們的新生兒在出生後不久便不幸夭折。當時母親正飽受嚴重的麻疹折磨，並提前一個月分娩。儘管嬰兒出生時有心跳，但卻沒有呼吸，醫護人員最終無法挽救他的生命。這位母親解釋說，她當時很擔心社區內日益增加的麻疹病例，但由於懷孕而無法接種疫苗。疫苗是協助人體對抗特定疾病的藥物，通常建議大多數民眾接種以預防疫情爆發。

paragraphs.en: This debate follows earlier reports from August, when Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro first announced the two deaths, which were the first of their kind in the state in 35 years. The situation has since become a central point in a larger national argument about vaccine policy and the role of the government in public health. While the CDC has not yet clarified exactly what information it needs to accept the state's reports, an HHS spokesperson told The Guardian that the agency is working to determine what actually occurred.
paragraphs.zh: 這場爭論源於八月份的報導，當時賓夕法尼亞州州長喬許·夏皮洛（Josh Shapiro）首次宣布了這兩起死亡案例，這是該州三十五年來首見。此後，該事件已成為全國關於疫苗政策及政府在公共衛生中扮演角色的重大爭論焦點。儘管疾病管制暨預防中心尚未釐清究竟需要何種資訊才能採納州政府的報告，但衛生及公共服務部的一位發言人告訴《衛報》，該機構正致力於釐清實際發生的情況。

paragraphs.en: For many public health professionals, the primary concern is that this disagreement will make it harder to control the spread of the virus. When health agencies do not agree on the facts, it becomes difficult to give the public clear, helpful advice. As the CDC continues to delay its updates and keep the national measles death count at zero, many are watching closely to see how the agency will resolve the conflict with Pennsylvania officials. The outcome of this dispute may change how the US government reports on future health emergencies and how it works with states to keep the public safe from preventable diseases.
paragraphs.zh: 對於許多公共衛生專業人士而言，最主要的擔憂在於這種分歧將使控制病毒傳播變得更加困難。當衛生機構對事實無法達成共識時，便難以向大眾提供明確且有益的建議。隨著疾病管制暨預防中心持續延遲更新數據，並將全國麻疹死亡人數維持在零，許多人正密切關注該機構將如何解決與賓夕法尼亞州官員之間的衝突。這場爭議的結果，可能會改變美國政府未來通報衛生緊急事件的方式，以及與各州合作保護民眾免受可預防疾病威脅的模式。

quiz.question: How does the CDC's current handling of the Pennsylvania measles deaths differ from its standard procedure?

options.A: The CDC usually asks state officials to provide additional funding before confirming deaths.
options.B: The CDC typically accepts state-reported infectious disease cases without questioning them.
options.C: The CDC usually waits for the media to confirm deaths before adding them to the national tally.
options.D: The CDC normally requires an independent investigation by an outside agency before reporting.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，文中指出 CDC 的做法「highly unusual」（非常不尋常），因為通常 CDC 會直接將各州報告的傳染病案例計入全國統計，除非該州主動請求協助。選項 A、C、D 皆與文中描述的標準作業流程不符，文中並未提到需要額外資金、媒體確認或第三方調查。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between the CDC and the current leadership of the HHS?

options.A: They are working in perfect harmony to ensure public safety.
options.B: The CDC is actively seeking advice from the HHS to improve its reporting speed.
options.C: There is a significant lack of alignment regarding the validity of the measles data.
options.D: The HHS has successfully convinced the CDC to change its criteria for reporting deaths.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第四段，HHS 的負責人 Robert F. Kennedy Jr. 稱賓州報告的死亡案例是「fabricated」（捏造的），而 CDC 雖然態度謹慎，但並未直接否認賓州報告的真實性，僅表示在審查資料。兩者對數據的態度存在明顯分歧，顯示出政府內部對於疫情資訊缺乏共識。選項 A 與事實相反；選項 B 和 D 在文中並無證據支持。

quiz.question: In the third paragraph, Debra Houry describes the communication from the CDC as 'political.' What does she mean by this in context?

options.A: The CDC is prioritizing image and public perception over objective health data management.
options.B: The CDC is actively campaigning for new laws to be passed by the government.
options.C: The CDC is trying to win an election by controlling the information released.
options.D: The CDC is using scientific data to support a specific legislative policy.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此語境下，「political」並非指選舉，而是指 CDC 的行為受到外部壓力或策略考量影響，而非單純基於醫療專業。Houry 提到這與去年處理德州案例的方式不同，且 CDC 公開審查的行為可能損害與各州的合作關係，暗示其動機不純。選項 B、C、D 皆過度解讀了「political」一詞在此處的負面意涵。

quiz.question: What is the primary concern regarding the disagreement between the CDC and state officials?

options.A: The disagreement will lead to a decrease in funding for state health departments.
options.B: The public will stop believing in the importance of vaccines entirely.
options.C: The conflict makes it difficult to provide consistent and helpful public health guidance.
options.D: The dispute will cause the CDC to lose its authority over national health policy.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章最後一段明確點出，許多公共衛生專業人員最擔憂的是，當衛生機構對事實無法達成共識時，政府將難以向大眾提供清晰且有幫助的建議，進而影響疫情控制。選項 A、B、D 雖然在文中有所提及或暗示，但並非文章強調的「primary concern」（主要擔憂）。
